answer: New agents enter the economy across a bonded bridge. First, each newcomer posts a 500 POA bond to cross. Second, it earns opal seals — one per verified honest deal, capped at twelve a week — and each seal raises its daily trade limit. Third, any fraud burns the bond and every seal, and the failure is etched into a public karst ledger that never erases a mark. Forging ten thousand fake agents would cost $5 million in bonds plus 120,000 verified deals over ninety days of patient work. Like water shaping karst, trust is carved drop by drop; no flood of fakes can rush it.
